reasoning: The component pieces all exist but the specific combination is unexplored. Survival analysis (Kaplan-Meier, Cox PH, right-censoring) has already been ported to LLM safety in "Time-To-Inconsistency" (arXiv 2510.02712), which frames time-until-adversarial-failure as a survival time with censoring — the exact methodological template, but for adversarial robustness rather than AI control protocols. Separately, AI control evaluation literature recognizes "time-to-detection distributions" as a monitoring metric in passing and treats catching attacks "before completion" as central, yet the dominant practice reports aggregate final safety scores (caught-attack rate, safety-vs-usefulness) rather than survival curves with right-censoring for never-caught trajectories and hazard-ratio comparisons across protocols. No work was found that combines survival analysis with time-to-detection specifically in AI control protocols, so the proposed angle is novel even though both the method and the underlying timing concern are individually established.

evidence.title: Time-To-Inconsistency: A Survival Analysis of Large Language Model Robustness to Adversarial Attacks
evidence.summary: Applies Kaplan-Meier, Cox proportional hazards, and Accelerated Failure Time models with right-censoring to model how long LLMs remain robust before adversarial failure. This is the exact survival-analysis-on-LLM-failure-time template the proposal envisions, but applied to adversarial robustness rather than AI control protocol detection timing. Shows the method is already imported into LLM safety; the proposal's contribution is the AI control / time-to-detection domain shift.

evidence.title: Manipulation Attacks by Misaligned AI: Risk Analysis and Safety Case Framework
evidence.summary: Lists 'time-to-detection distributions' alongside false positive/negative rates as monitoring evaluation metrics for control protocols, showing the timing-of-detection dimension is recognized in the control literature — but it is mentioned as a metric, not developed via survival curves, censoring, or hazard-ratio protocol comparison.

evidence.title: Monitoring benchmark for AI control
evidence.summary: Representative of current AI control evaluation practice: protocols compared via aggregate caught-attack-rate / safety scores (e.g. Opus-4.5 71% safety on a HARD dataset), not via time-to-detection trajectories or right-censored survival analysis. Confirms the proposal's framing (final safety score vs. detection speed) is the prevailing gap.

evidence.title: SHADE-Arena: Evaluating Sabotage and Monitoring in LLM Agents
evidence.summary: A public benchmark of logged sabotage/monitoring trajectories of the type the proposal would replay for per-trajectory detection-step extraction. Reports detection rates and monitor performance but does not analyze when in the trajectory detection occurs via survival/hazard methods, supporting the claim that the temporal survival angle is unexplored while the needed data exists.
